FN-OD1KMM-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 154
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Will Barfoot
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/12/2023
Senate Bill 154 as reported by the Committee on Judiciary provides for the suspension of a
driver's license by the court, under certain conditions, for (1) violation of written bond to appear
or failure to appear in court for any pre-adjudication court date or trial date, (2) failure to appear
in court for a traffic violation post adjudication compliance review, or (3) failure to pay at least
6 court ordered payments for fines, fees, or court costs as a result of a traffic violation.
Further the provisions of this bill could also reduce receipts to the various funds that court costs,
fines, and fees are distributed to, by an undetermined amount, dependent upon the number of
individuals that fail to pay court costs, fines, and fees, pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
In addition, this bill could increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Law
Enforcement Agency and the Supreme Court of Alabama to adopt rules to implement the
provisions of this bill.

FN-OD1KMM-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 154
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Senator Will Barfoot
Security
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 05/03/2023
Senate Bill 154 as reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland Security provides
for the suspension of a driver's license by the court, under certain conditions, for (1) violation of
written bond to appear or failure to appear in court for any pre-adjudication court date or trial
date, (2) failure to appear in court for a traffic violation post adjudication compliance review, or
(3) failure to pay at least 3 court ordered payments for fines, fees, or court costs as a result of a
traffic violation.
This bill would also provide for the reinstatement of driving privileges upon compliance with
the notice to appear and payment of the reinstatement fee.
Further the provisions of this bill could also reduce receipts to the various funds that court costs,
fines, and fees are distributed to, by an undetermined amount, dependent upon the number of
individuals that fail to pay court costs, fines, and fees, pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
In addition, this bill could increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Law
Enforcement Agency and the Supreme Court of Alabama to adopt rules to implement the
provisions of this bill.
